title: Stocks Break Losing Streak as Chipmakers Rebound While Traders Brace For The First Midterm Results
detail:
Stocks Break Losing Streak as Chipmakers Rebound While Traders Brace For The First Midterm Results
Demian Bio
Tue, November 3, 2026 at 4:16 PM EST 3 min read
^DJI
^GSPC
^IXIC

Stocks climbed on Tuesday, breaking a three-day losing streak as chipmakers rebounded and traders braced for the first results of the midterm elections.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 0.38%, while the S&P 500 gained 0.36% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite overperformed, gaining 0.83%.

Traders are looking at the electoral results to react on Wednesday, with some sectors being particularly exposed to political developments.

Artificial intelligence stocks have come under pressure, while questions about regulation, government spending and the conflict with Iran threaten to complicate the market's historically strong performance after midterms.

The election could prove particularly consequential for companies tied to AI infrastructure. Investors are watching whether Democratic gains would strengthen efforts to restrict data centers or reconsider incentives supporting their construction.

Texas, a major center for the expansion, is an important test. Marcus said an unexpected defeat for Republican Gov. Greg Abbott could unsettle investors concerned about the industry's political support.

Goldman Sachs strategists, however, see limits to the potential disruption. They believe a Democratic Congress could curb data center tax incentives, while a nationwide moratorium remains unlikely under any election outcome.

Health care could move in the opposite direction. Investors anticipate Democrats would seek to restore enhanced Affordable Care Act premium subsidies and revisit Medicaid changes enacted under Republicans. Those priorities could improve expectations for hospitals and health insurers, although passing legislation would still require navigating the White House.

Beyond individual sectors, investors must weigh whether the usual post-election rally will materialize. The S&P 500 finished higher one year after every midterm election from 1982 through 2022, according to CNBC's historical analysis.

In the geopolitical sphere, U.S.-Iran negotiations appeared to hit a snag after Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said that Washington's latest response to the proposal to cease hostilities was "not convincing."

"They must fully and explicitly address Iran's seven conditions and act upon them; only in this case will the Strait of Hormuz be reopened," Rezaei said in a social media publication.

The remarks come shortly after an Iranian official also said a deal with the U.S. is still elusive. Speaking at a news briefing, the official, who remained anonymous, said "mediators are working hard to narrow gaps between Tehran and Washington." However, he noted that "Tehran's conditions must be met if the U.S. wants Hormuz reopened."

What History Says

12 months out: The S&P 500 has never been negative in the 12 months after a midterm since 1950. The average gain is about 14.8%. Read more (Oct 19, 2026)

Longer window: One analysis measured from the last full week before the election to the end of the following year, about 14 months. The index rose in all 19 cycles, with an average gain of +20.3% and a median of +22.3%. The weakest was +1.3%. Read more (Nov 3, 2026)

UBS view: Late August through March averaged +14.5%. Choppy trading usually comes first, with a median decline of 1.4% into early October. Only 1978, 2002 and 2018 were negative over that window. Read more (Sep 20, 2026)

Divided government: The S&P 500 finished the year positive in 92.3% of divided-government periods, with an average return of 17%. The same article notes the index has gone more than 1,000 days without a new 52-week low.

The short-term caveat: The index was higher one week after 14 of 19 elections. By week two, only 10 of 19 were positive. After one month it was 15 of 19. A retracement in week two is common. Read more (Nov 2, 2026)

Investing.com -- The Santa Claus rally window is still seven weeks away. It covers the final five trading days of December plus the first two of January. Thinking about it now isn't premature, but there's little signal in it yet. It's a short seasonal pattern, not a forecast.

What history says

Base rate: The S&P 500 has been positive in this window in roughly 75% of years since the 1950s, with average gains of about 1.4%. Read more (Dec 29, 2025)

Recent record: The rally missed in 2024, when the S&P 500 returned -0.9% over the window. Read more (Dec 25, 2025)

Last year: Hopes faded again as stocks drifted lower into year-end. Fairlead's Katie Stockton said the rally "came early." Read more (Dec 30, 2025)

Wider seasonality: Q4 has historically been the strongest quarter, rising about 80% of the time. November and December usually do the heavy lifting. Read more (Aug 21, 2026)

Where we stand now

S&P 500 (US500): 7,562.35 (+0.27%) as of Nov 3, 3:00 PM EST || 1W: -2.08% || YTD: +9.95% || 52W high: 7,844.52

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

The index sits about 3.6% below its 52-week high. It also gave back 2.08% over the past week, so it enters the seasonally strong stretch after a wobble, not at a peak. A pullback before the strong months is the pattern bulls usually want. It isn't a guarantee, though.

Bull and bear cases

Bull: The year is up about 10%, the seasonal tailwind is real, and the index has room to retest highs.

Bear: A few things could undercut the pattern:

The last two windows were weak.

Leadership has been narrow.

Year-end liquidity is thin, which exaggerates moves in both directions.

The takeaway is that this is a tilt in the odds, not a catalyst. Earnings, policy and rates will matter more than the calendar. The seasonal edge can be wiped out by a macro surprise, as in 2022.

The S&P 500 has been falling recently, as have many top dividend stocks. While that may be bad news for people who own those stocks, for investors looking to buy or to add to their positions, that can be great news, as it means more deals are available in the markets these days.

Even if the short-term outlook may not look all that great for the markets or the economy as a whole, it can still make sense to invest right now and hold for the long haul. Three excellent dividend stocks that look cheap this month and that offer high yields are AT&T (NYSE:T), Novo Nordisk (NYSE:NVO), and Vici Properties (NYSE:VICI). Here's why these are stocks worth buying right now.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

AT&T

Telecom giant AT&T offers a fairly high yield of 5.2%, which is more than four times the S&P 500 average of only 1.1%. That's a ton more dividend income for investors who crave recurring payouts.

This year hasn't been a great one for the telecom stock, as it's down 14%, and a big reason for that may be due to concerns that Space Exploration Technologies Corp will disrupt its operations with its aspiration of Starlink becoming a major mobile carrier in the near future.

Those concerns, however, I believe, are overblown. AT&T is still performing exceptionally well, and it could take years before Starlink becomes a significant rival. Even then, AT&T has been no stranger to competition over the years and has continued to do well. Selling the stock based on those fears is premature, to say the least. Buying this top telecom stock right now, while it's trading near its 52-week low, could be a great move.

Novo Nordisk

Another struggling dividend stock that looks enticing to buy on the dip right now is Novo Nordisk, the drugmaker that makes Ozempic and Wegovy. Its GLP-1 drugs are highly popular, but rising competition with longtime rival Eli Lilly has hurt the company's growth rate and its share price. This year, it's down 20% thus far.

However, the business is by no means doomed, and a recent trial showed that a higher dose version of Wegovy resulted in some patients losing up to 28% of their weight, putting it in the same ballpark as Zepbound -- Eli Lilly's leading weight loss drug.

While the market has written off Novo Nordisk and remains bearish on it, I believe it's become an incredibly underrated, dirt cheap stock to buy not only for its growth potential but also its dividend. Due to the stock's 30% decline over the past five years, it's now yielding 4.4%. Meanwhile, the healthcare stock trades at just 10 times its trailing earnings.

Cerebras Systems (CBRS) stock fell 57.6% from August 4 to November 2, 2026, while the S&P 500 lost 2.3%. Shares slid following the company's August 12 second-quarter report, and they dropped again in late September and early October as reports said Cerebras lost an OpenAI workload to Nvidia. The price appears to assume Cerebras's growth is less secure than it looked, so how much of that growth depends on OpenAI?

Much Of Cerebras's Backlog Comes From OpenAI

A large part of the business Cerebras has already signed depends on OpenAI. The company had $25.4 billion of contracted work still to deliver at June 30. On the August 12 call, management said none of it came from AWS or any other large cloud provider. September news reports said a significant amount of that backlog traces to a December agreement with OpenAI.

Management said on that same call that OpenAI will still be a meaningful portion of revenue in 2027, and that share will shrink over time as AWS and other customers grow.

The late-September news concerned the customer behind much of that backlog. News reports that week, including on October 2, said Cerebras lost a key workload for OpenAI's Ultrafast mode to Nvidia during the same week a lockup on early holders' shares expired. On October 5, OpenAI's chief executive called Cerebras a close partner, and the shares rose 11% in early trading. They still lost 42.1% between October 2 and November 2. Late in October, short seller Culper Research disclosed a position against Cerebras, and the shares fell 11.7% to a record low on November 2.

Cerebras Reported A Far Wider Loss In August

The losses have not narrowed yet. Cerebras reported revenue of $180 million for the quarter ended June 30, up from $103 million a year earlier but below the $193 million reported for the three months to March 31. The company's operating loss grew to $477 million from $15 million in the prior quarter, though management's own core operating loss was far smaller at $33.6 million. Gross margin fell to 14.2% from 44.6% three months earlier. News reports said the shares slumped more than 18% before trading opened on August 13 after the company missed key estimates.

On that core measure, revenue rose 103% to $209.9 million, but management expects weaker third-quarter margins. The company guided core operating margin to minus 25% to minus 23%, against minus 16% in the second quarter. For the full year, management raised its core revenue outlook to $880 million to $890 million. Management also called the third quarter the low point for core gross margin, with an improvement in the fourth as more of its own lower-cost systems come online.

Expedia (EXPE) raised its revenue forecast for fiscal 2026 on August 5, 2026, yet the stock has slipped 6.3% from its August 5 close, the last before that after-market release, through November 2, against a 2.4% fall for the S&P 500. A higher forecast alongside a weaker share price is a mixed signal, and the chart is worth checking before taking the raise at face value. So where does Expedia's share price stand today against its own averages?

Expedia Stock Backs The Raise Only In Part

Expedia's share price stands above both of its main averages. The stock closed at $298.99 on November 2, above its 50-day average of $285.69, the average closing price over the last 50 trading days. That 50-day average sits above the 200-day average of $258.50, the same measure over 200 trading days, leaving the stock's uptrend intact on its averages.

The stock's return since the release does not align with the raise. Expedia reported after the market closed on August 5. On August 6, the first session after the release, the stock fell 4.1% while the S&P 500 slipped 0.2%, a move that priced the second-quarter results and the raised forecast together. Much of the strength above the averages is recent: over the month to November 2, Expedia stock returned 12.8%, including dividends, against a 2.3% loss for the S&P 500.

What Expedia Raised For Fiscal 2026

Management raised its fiscal 2026 revenue forecast to a range of $16.05 billion to $16.22 billion. At the midpoint, that is 2.1% above the $15.8 billion it guided in May. Management tied the raise to the strength of the first half and its assumptions for the third quarter.

That strength showed in the second quarter, when revenue grew 14% from a year earlier, a pace management said beat its own expectations. The business-to-business segment, which serves more than 70,000 partners, posted its 20th straight quarter of double-digit growth.

The raise went beyond revenue. Management lifted its fiscal 2026 forecast for gross bookings, the value of travel booked through Expedia, to $130 billion at the midpoint from $128 billion. It also now expects its adjusted EBITDA margin, its own measure of earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization as a share of revenue, to widen by 1.6 percentage points over last year at the midpoint, up from 1.1 points.

What Could Move Expedia Stock From Here?

A much slower second half would still meet the raised forecast. At its midpoint, the raised forecast leaves Expedia needing about $8.39 billion in the third and fourth quarters of fiscal 2026, or 5.5% more than in the same quarters a year earlier. That compares with 14.3% growth in the first half. For the third quarter, management guided revenue growth of about 5% to 8% and said it expects bookings growth to moderate as Expedia laps faster growth from a year earlier.

title: What Did Reddit's Quarter Change For Its Stock?

What Did Reddit's Quarter Change For Its Stock?

Reddit (RDDT) stock fell 29.2% on October 30, 2026, during the first trading session after its fiscal Q3 2026 report. The S&P 500 lost 1.8% on the same day. This marks a steep fall following a quarter where revenue of $895 million came in about 2% above what analysts had expected. So what did Reddit tell investors that its results did not?

Reddit Warned Of A Drop In Daily Users

During the October 29 call, management said daily users could fall by a low double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter from a current base of 130 million. The warning came from search. Traffic that search engines send to Reddit fell meaningfully in fiscal Q3 2026, and the decline sped up late in the quarter. In October, those referrals dropped by more than 1 million a week on average, and management's estimate for users assumes that pace continues.

The results themselves held no surprise of that size. Earnings per share came in at $1.40, above the $1.33 analysts expected. Reddit's peers fell far less on the same day. Meta Platforms fell 1.5% and Alphabet fell 1.4%, while Pinterest, the weakest of the three peers, fell 2.8%. The fall was Reddit's own, not its industry's.

Is Reddit's Slowdown More Than One Quarter?

It is for sales growth. Reddit's revenue grew 69.1% from a year earlier in fiscal Q1 2026, a shade below the 69.7% posted in fiscal Q4 2025. Growth then slowed to 61.1% in fiscal Q2 2026 and to 53.0% in fiscal Q3 2026. Management expects growth to slow again in fiscal Q4 2026, forecasting revenue of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, or 38% to 42% growth. News reports on October 30 said that outlook was lower than expected. The traffic warning is new, but the slower growth is not.

Profitability is another matter. Reddit reported an operating margin of 29.2% in fiscal Q3 2026, compared with 23.7% a year earlier.

Management argued that Reddit is still growing where it counts: engagement from its app and logged-in users. About 80% of Reddit's monetization happens within that group, management said. The company added that Reddit is still a top search term in Google, and that Google is simply not sending people to Reddit the way it used to.

When Will Reddit's User Count Be Known?

The fiscal Q4 2026 results will be Reddit's first report since the warning. During that quarter, management plans to begin fully testing a logged-in-only version of Reddit in select markets outside the U.S. The company said the change would likely trade reach for engagement, noting that it will keep evaluating how it reports users.
